text.title: C# Clean Architecture + CQRS Worked Examples
text.summary: One use-case worked through every layer — the solution tree, the aggregate, the command/handler/validator/response quartet, the one-line controller — plus the antipatterns each example replaces and the manifest the methodology emits.

example.code: src/ ├── Faion.Domain/ │ └── Orders/ │ ├── Order.cs # aggregate, no public setters │ └── Events/OrderShipped.cs # domain event record ├── Faion.Application/ │ └── Orders/ShipOrder/ │ ├── ShipOrderCommand.cs # record : IRequest<ShipOrderResponse> │ ├── ShipOrderHandler.cs # the only IRequestHandler for it │ ├── ShipOrderValidator.cs # AbstractValidator<ShipOrderCommand> │ └── ShipOrderResponse.cs # response record ├── Faion.Infrastructure/ │ └── Orders/OrderRepository.cs # EF Core impl of IOrderRepository └── Faion.Api/ └── Controllers/OrdersController.cs # one-line mediator dispatch
example.note: One folder per use-case (one-command-per-folder). `Faion.Domain.csproj` carries no PackageReference to EF Core or ASP.NET Core; `Faion.Api.csproj` references Application + Infrastructure only (layer-direction).

Every setter is private and every transition is guarded inside the method that performs it (rich-domain-no-setters, behaviour-in-entities). Events are raised where the state changed and can be cleared after publish (domain-events-raised-and-cleared).

antipattern.description: `order.Status = "shipped";` from a handler, with `public OrderStatus Status { get; set; }` on the entity.
antipattern.reason: The invariant "a cancelled order cannot ship" has no place to live; every caller re-implements it, or nobody does.

example.note: Record request implementing IRequest<T>, exactly one handler, `Handle` takes the CancellationToken (cqrs-record-request-per-handler). The handler orchestrates and the rule lives on the aggregate. Validation runs in the pipeline before this code, so there is no `if (req.Carrier == null)` here (validators-on-commands). No DbContext, no HttpContext (dbcontext-behind-interface).

Explicit, commented behaviour order asserted by a test (pipeline-behaviour-order). The action is a dispatch and a return — no mapping, no auth check, no header parsing (controller-with-logic is the failure this prevents).
